clips.text_en_b1: Alrighty, in one of the best moments of my life, I managed to hack into my own dogecoin wallet from 2014. It held 730,000 DOGE that I had forgotten the password to. That is about $60,000 USD. I feel it can become a lot more with prudent investments. Real estate is pricy in my area, so a fixer-upper ready for sale may work.

clips.text_en_b2: This might genuinely be one of the best moments of my life so far, since I finally managed to crack my own dogecoin wallet from 2014. It held around 730,000 DOGE that I had completely forgotten the password to, worth roughly $60,000 USD at current prices. Real estate is brutal in my area, so a fixer-upper I could flip quickly sounds ideal, although I am open to other suggestions too. What would you do, /biz/?
clips.text_en_c1: Against all odds, I somehow managed to regain access to a dormant dogecoin wallet I had originally set up back in 2014, which still held a staggering 730,000 DOGE that I had long since forgotten about. At prevailing market rates, that amounts to roughly $60,000 USD, and if I exercise any degree of prudence with how I deploy the capital, I am convinced the figure could appreciate considerably. Real estate in my region remains prohibitively expensive, so a modestly priced fixer-upper that I could subsequently flip might constitute the most viable avenue. Thoughts, /biz/?
clips.text_en_c2: In what can only be described as a serendipitous turn of fate, I somehow managed to crack the password to my own dormant 2014 Dogecoin wallet, an asset I had long since written off as irretrievably lost to the digital ether. Lo and behold, the balance read a scarcely believable 730,000 DOGE, which, given the prevailing market rate, translates to roughly sixty thousand United States dollars. Given that property prices in my locale remain prohibitively inflated, I am seriously entertaining the notion of acquiring a modest fixer-upper, doing it up, and flipping it for a respectable profit.

clips.text_zh: 今日biz有人問點解個個都係BTC升咗15%之後先衝 入嚟 我自己都係廢物 永遠都係後知後覺 個倉又係輸緊 命理話我今年唔應該trade 但我邊忍得住 thx
clips.text_en_b1: Why buy BTC after the pump? You watch BTC do nothing for weeks, then ignore it completely. Suddenly it pumps 15% and everyone wants in. Why does everyone want to buy after the move already happened? This came up on /biz/ today and it stings because half of us did exactly that.
clips.source_hint: Anons complain about chasing BTC after a 15% move

signal.rationale: Post-hoc complaint about chasing, no fresh setup, mostly FOMO regret

clips.text_en_b2: Why do people keep buying BTC after the pump? You watch it flatline for weeks on end, ignore it entirely, and the moment it finally jumps 15% everyone piles in. A thread on /biz/ brought this up today, and it stings because half of us did exactly that, myself included. Meanwhile my position is bleeding red and astrology insists I should not be trading this year, yet here I am anyway.
clips.text_en_c1: It is a question that recurs with almost wearying predictability: why does the retail crowd invariably feel compelled to chase Bitcoin only after it has already appreciated by some 15%? You watch the chart stagnate for weeks on end, dismiss it as boring, and look away, only for the moment you stop paying attention to be precisely when the breakout occurs. This was the topic on /biz/ today, and frankly it stings because half of us, myself included, fell squarely into that exact trap. Astrology warned me not to trade this year, yet discipline was never my strong suit.
clips.text_en_c2: A thread on /biz/ today raised a question that, for all its surface banality, cuts to the very heart of speculative psychology: why is it that retail participants invariably demonstrate such an exquisite talent for buying Bitcoin precisely after the substantial move has already materialised? The pattern is, by now, almost tediously familiar; weeks of consolidation elicit yawns and indifference, the charts stagnate, sentiment sours, and then, the moment a decisive fifteen percent rally crystallises, the very same cohort that dismissed the asset as moribund scrambles aboard with unseemly alacrity. It stings, I must confess, precisely because half of us, myself emphatically included, have committed this exact folly with metronomic regularity.

clips.text_en_b1: Snailcats win again. In 2016, the godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton predicted that AI would replace radiologists within 5 years, maybe 10 years tops. It is now 10 years later and there are more radiologists now, in higher demand, making much higher salaries than in 2016. Next up to embarrass himself on the world stage: Elon Musk.
clips.source_hint: Anons dunk on Hinton's 2016 radiologist prediction

signal.rationale: Cultural commentary on AI predictions, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Snailcats strike again. Back in 2016, the so-called godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton, confidently predicted that AI would replace radiologists within five years, possibly stretching to ten. It has now been a full decade, yet there are actually more radiologists than before, in greater demand and earning significantly higher salaries. That gives the rest of us licence to mock doomers. My guess for the next public embarrassment on the world stage: Elon Musk.
clips.text_en_c1: Snailcats triumph once more. Back in 2016, the so-called godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton, publicly predicted that radiologists would be rendered obsolete within a five-to-ten-year window as deep learning matured. Fast forward a decade and the reality could hardly be more damning for that forecast: the radiology workforce has expanded, demand for specialists has surged, and compensation has climbed appreciably relative to 2016 levels. If humiliation were a competitive sport, Elon Musk would appear to be the next contender queued up for a similar public reckoning.
clips.text_en_c2: Once again, the prognostications of our self-appointed AI savants have been comprehensively vindicated by the cold, indifferent passage of time. In 2016, Geoffrey Hinton, the so-called godfather of the field, declared with characteristic authority that artificial intelligence would render radiologists obsolete within a mere five years, perhaps stretching to a generous decade. A decade has now elapsed, and the radiologist, far from being consigned to the dustbin of professional history, has become more numerous, more sought-after, and considerably better remunerated than at the moment of Hinton's pronouncement. The cognitive dissonance required to maintain such confidently incorrect public positions remains, to my mind, one of the more extraordinary spectacles of our era. One suspects, rather uncharitably, that Elon Musk is merely biding his time before contributing his own memorable contribution to this venerable tradition.

clips.text_en_b1: A 44-year-old NEET killed eight relatives, including four children, as they gathered for Sunday dinner in Billings, Montana, just weeks after his parents forced him to move out. A family member told AP the shooter was 44-year-old Alan Smith. Smith's parents had asked him to move out, but he returned on Sunday and opened fire on the family.
clips.source_hint: NEET kills family after being told to move out

signal.rationale: News tragedy, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: A 44-year-old NEET allegedly shot dead eight relatives, including four children, while they were gathered for Sunday dinner in Billings, Montana. Family members identified the gunman as 44-year-old Alan Smith, who had only recently been forced by his parents to move out. He returned on Sunday and opened fire on everyone at the table. Honestly, the whole thing left me feeling completely numb, like someone had dumped ice water over my head.
clips.text_en_c1: A truly harrowing item surfaced on /pol/ today. In Billings, Montana, a 44-year-old NEET who had recently been compelled by his parents to vacate the family home returned during a Sunday dinner gathering and opened fire, killing eight relatives, four of whom were children. A family member confirmed to the Associated Press that the shooter has been identified as Alan Smith. The details, which read like something out of a tragedy, are the sort that leave you staring blankly at the screen for an uncomfortably long while afterwards.
clips.text_en_c2: A particularly grim thread on /pol/ has been doing the rounds, detailing a tragedy that defies easy comprehension. A forty-four-year-old NEET, having been pressed by his parents to vacate the family home, allegedly returned to the property during a routine Sunday dinner and proceeded to gun down eight relatives, among them four children. The sheer, nauseating banality of the setting, a family gathered around a table sharing a meal, only amplifies the horror, transforming what ought to be the most innocuous of domestic rituals into something grotesque and irreparable. The shooter has been identified by an AP source as Alan Smith. As a thirty-something singleton navigating the precarious straits of a deeply uncertain future, I found the account viscerally unsettling, a cold shower of the most unwelcome variety.

clips.text_en_b2: A Norwegian retailer, Elkjop, has listed Monolith Soft as the developer behind a Zelda Ocarina of Time remake heading to Switch 2, product code 1115379. This lines up with earlier evidence, including a leaked controller logo that matches Monolith's branding and their recruitment history. Nintendo has stayed silent so far, as usual, but honestly I would rather grind LoL Season 15 than wait another decade for another Zelda release.
clips.text_en_c1: Yet another piece of corroborating evidence has emerged regarding the long-rumoured Zelda Ocarina of Time remake. The Norwegian retailer Elkjop has, apparently, listed Monolith Soft as the developer of the Switch 2 title under product code 1115379, which dovetails neatly with the previously leaked controller branding and the studio's historical recruitment patterns. Nintendo, characteristically, has declined to issue any official confirmation. Personally, I would rather grind out another season of League than wait indefinitely for this remake to materialise.
clips.text_en_c2: Further corroboration has emerged regarding the long-rumoured Ocarina of Time remake, and frankly, my enthusiasm for the project is outweighed only by my dwindling patience. The Norwegian retailer Elkjop has, in a listing subsequently flagged across /v/, attributed development to Monolith Soft, with the product page specifying a Switch 2 SKU under catalogue code 1115379. This ought to be read in conjunction with the leaked controller artwork, which bore a striking resemblance to Microsoft's design language, alongside the studio's well-documented recruitment patterns. Nintendo, predictably, has offered no official comment. One can only hope the wait proves worth it, though at this juncture, personally, I would sooner endure the slings and arrows of League of Legends Season 15 than endure yet another indeterminate development cycle for a remaster of a twenty-seven-year-old masterpiece.

clips.text_en_b2: Picrel is what I look like after two years of consistent lifting. I am 5'9, sitting at 160 lbs, having started as a 140 lb skinnyfat mess, bulked up to 200, and cut back down to where I am now. clips.text_en_c1: Pictured is my current physique after two years of fairly consistent effort. I stand 5'9 and currently weigh in at 160 lbs, having begun my journey at a rather unremarkable 140 lbs in a decidedly skinnyfat state, bulked aggressively up to 200 lbs, and subsequently cut back down to where I am now. Given that my frame is on the narrower side, I have deliberately prioritised shoulder development to create the illusion of width. My current nutrition sits at approximately 160g protein, 272g carbohydrates and 57g fat for a daily intake of 2,293 calories, supplemented by ten thousand-plus steps and occasional cardio. I would welcome any suggestions regarding split optimisation.
clips.text_en_c2: Pictured is the rather unremarkable result of two years spent intermittently but earnestly pursuing the iron game, a journey whose vicissitudes I shall now inflict upon the assembled readership. My measurements, for the morbidly curious, stand at five foot nine and a comparatively modest one hundred and sixty pounds, a figure arrived at via the well-trodden path from a thoroughly unenviable skinnyfat baseline of one hundred and forty pounds, followed by a fairly aggressive bulk to two hundred, and an altogether more measured cut back down to the present. Given that my skeletal frame remains stubbornly narrow despite every conceivable assault upon it, I have elected to accord disproportionate priority to shoulder development, seeking through sheer volume of work to manufacture the optical illusion of breadth.

clips.text_en_b2: Now that Railgun has wrapped up, I am personally planning to track down every English physical release in the franchise: Railgun, Astral Buddy, Accelerator, Mental Out, and Index. Once the Index manga finishes, though, I am essentially done with the series altogether. Between grinding through HKIE textbooks and having zero time for games or anime, my guilty pleasure has basically evaporated. At least I finally picked up this volume in the picture.
clips.text_en_c1: Now that the Railgun manga has officially concluded, I find myself compelled to take stock of what remains of this sprawling franchise and, more importantly, decide where to channel whatever lingering affection I still harbour for it. My own plan, which I suspect will prove rather costly, is to methodically acquire every available English-language physical release: Railgun, Astral Buddy, Accelerator, Mental Out, and of course Index. Once that final Index volume sees print, however, I intend to wash my hands of the lot entirely. The pictured volume arrived just yesterday, and I could not be more pleased.
clips.text_en_c2: With the Railgun arc having at last drawn to a close, a thread on /a/ solicited reflections on personal disposition toward the franchise, and the responses, predictably, ranged from the dutifully nostalgic to the openly exasperated. My own intentions, for what they are worth, involve the systematic accumulation of every available English-language physical volume, encompassing not merely the eponymous Railgun but also Astral Buddy, the Accelerator spinoff, Mental Out, and, naturally, the original Index manga in its entirety. Once that particular wellspring runs dry, however, I intend to divest myself entirely; the franchise, for all its considerable charms, has long since ceased to justify the emotional investment it demands.
